clue.text: After setback, old boy's given a hint for rowing event

indicators.note: a setback sends something backwards, so the abbreviation for old boy is turned round

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil of a school
a trace is a tiny hint or suggestion of something

explanation.surface: A former pupil recovers from a setback and is tipped off about a rowing race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After setback' turns OB into BO. The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boat Race is the famous annual rowing contest between Oxford and Cambridge universities.

clue.text: Argue I should be replaced by European tennis star

indicators.note: the clue tells us the letter I must give way to another letter in the word for argue

parts.note: to bicker is to argue in a petty way

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop quarrelling and make way for a top European tennis player.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'I' is the letter itself, swapped for E in BICKER. Boris Becker is the German player who won Wimbledon at seventeen.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Becker is a German former world number one, a three-time Wimbledon champion.

clue.text: Indian swiftly catches horse

indicators.note: one word catching another holds it inside itself, so the letter for horse goes within

parts.note: apace is an old-fashioned word meaning swiftly
H is slang for heroin, known as horse, and a standard crossword abbreviation

explanation.surface: A Native American rider quickly lassoes a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people of the south-western United States, an Indian nation in older usage.

clue.text: Man given stick, crossing unfinished part of motorway

indicators.note: the stick goes across the other piece, standing either side of it, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a rod is a stick or pole

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a lane is one strip of a motorway's carriageway

explanation.surface: A man with a walking stick crosses a half-built stretch of motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts LANE to LAN, which goes inside ROD.
explanation.definitionFit: Roland is a man's first name, so a man can stand for it in crosswords.

clue.text: Acceptable behaviour in political meeting

explanation.surface: Good manners are on display at a party gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Social norms of acceptable conduct are customs; a party's large formal assembly, as in US politics, is also called this.

clue.text: A bit harassed? Answer — order a cab

indicators.note: only a bit of the word harassed is used, its opening letter

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A stressed person gives a hurried reply and calls for a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit' takes the H from harassed. OM stands for the Order of Merit, an honour in the gift of the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom is a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, the forerunner of the taxi.

clue.text: Agreed a Conservative landslide implies this?

explanation.surface: Someone nods along to the idea of a sweeping Tory election victory.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase as two words: a landslide means everyone, in a vote, went to the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'fine, yes' signals agreement; a huge Conservative win would mean every voter went to the right wing.

clue.text: In farmyard enclosures, resting place for baby dogs

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, the baby's bed placed within the pig pens

parts.note: sties are pens for pigs on a farm
a cot is a baby's bed

explanation.surface: In the farmyard pens, there's a bed for the pups.
explanation.walkthrough: COT goes inside STIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotties is the familiar name for Scottish terriers, a breed of small dog.

clue.text: Average price of fashion?

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A shopper asks what clothes typically cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Price of fashion' gives fashion's price, so MODE comes before RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate means middling or medium, neither high nor low.

clue.text: Telephone service disrupted in chalet

indicators.note: disrupted letters are thrown out of order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A phone line goes down at a ski lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges INCHALET.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatline is a phone service where callers pay to talk with others.

clue.text: Old man, crazy nut

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters going wild, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly man is called a nutcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' looks like an insult for the old man, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond is the edible seed of a tree related to the peach, sold as a nut.

clue.text: Luck, though initially lacking, in the end is much improved

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another, the shortened luck sitting within the end

parts.note: end is the end, taken as a word

indicators.note: lacking the first letter, so the word for luck loses its opening letter

parts.note: chance is luck or fortune

explanation.surface: A gambler's fortune, poor at first, turns out much better in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially lacking' trims CHANCE to HANCE, and 'in' puts it inside END.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enhanced has been raised in quality or value, made better.

clue.text: Worker's reduced profit — terrible

indicators.note: the words are cut down at each end, leaving a run of letters from inside them

explanation.surface: A labourer complains that a pay cut has been dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' strips 'profit terrible' to the letters across its middle, FIT and TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitter is a skilled tradesperson who assembles or installs machinery or parts.

clue.text: Dad tore head cover, and mum's in such a state

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
rent is the past tense of rend, meaning tore
a hood is a covering for the head

explanation.surface: A father rips his hat while the mother is in a fluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum's in such a state' looks like an upset mother, but it is the condition of being a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a mother or father is the condition of raising children, the state both parents share.

clue.text: -E-mail message might be sent with such affection?

definitions.text: -E-mail message might be sent with such

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if an email can carry warm feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affection' leads to fondness; the other sense is the file sent along with an email.
explanation.definitionFit: A file appended to an email is one; an emotional bond or fondness for someone is also called this.

clue.text: One way to murder, clutching old iron?

indicators.note: the method of killing holds the letter for old tight inside it

parts.note: to smother someone is to suffocate them, a way of killing

explanation.surface: A killer wonders whether to use an antique iron as the weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron' looks like a murder weapon in the surface, but it is the definition: an iron flattens creases.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a household tool that flattens creases out of fabric, so it is something that evens things out.

clue.text: Pantiles damaged? Couldn't be more obvious

indicators.note: damaged tiles are broken up, so the letters of pantiles are rearranged

explanation.surface: The broken roof tiles are there for everyone to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges PANTILES; pantiles are curved roof tiles.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of plain, meaning clear, is the most evident, as clear as it can be.

clue.text: Entitles criminal to become used to new development

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook claims rights while adapting to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges ENTITLES.
explanation.definitionFit: To get comfortable in new surroundings or circumstances is to adapt to them.

clue.text: Considered linking Scottish island to eastern port

parts.note: Mull is an island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland
Dover is a port in Kent on the English Channel

explanation.surface: Planners weigh up a ferry route from a Scottish island to an English harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: DOVER is the Kent ferry port facing France.
explanation.definitionFit: To think something over carefully is to ponder it, so thought-over ideas have been pondered.

clue.text: Soak and wipe clean

explanation.surface: Instructions for washing up: drench it, then wipe it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' here is a noun: a scrounger who lives off others.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrounger who lives off others is a cadger; to wipe with a porous pad is to clean a surface.

clue.text: Chief mostly accepts what's been decreed for republic

indicators.note: the shortened word takes the other piece in, holding it inside itself
mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: main means chief or principal
a law is a rule decreed by authority

explanation.surface: A head of state largely goes along with official decrees in his country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims MAIN to MAI, and 'accepts' puts LAW inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked country in south-east Africa, governed as a republic since 1966.

clue.text: Boot that is found at bottom of shaft

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits under the first, at its foot

parts.note: a well is a shaft sunk into the ground
ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A boot is discovered lying at the foot of a well.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'found at bottom of' places IE under WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellie is short for wellington, a waterproof rubber boot.

clue.text: Almost half of church members rejected poets

indicators.note: nearly half of the long word is involved, four of its ten letters
rejected letters are thrown out, so that part of the word is removed

parts.note: Methodists are members of the Methodist church

explanation.surface: Nearly half the congregation turned down the poets.
explanation.walkthrough: METH, four of METHODISTS' ten letters, is removed, leaving the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of odes, formal lyric poems, are poets of that particular kind.

clue.text: Strike, and this will be deducted from wage

definitions.text: this will be deducted from wage

explanation.surface: Workers walk out and lose pay as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: A stoppage is also a deduction taken from pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkout halts work; a sum withheld from pay is also called this.

clue.text: Vet, maybe, called out for dog

indicators.note: something called out is spoken aloud, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a vet is one kind of healer, someone who cures

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for the vet when the dog is ill.
explanation.walkthrough: A heeler is an Australian cattle dog that nips at the heels of livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A heeler is a herding dog bred to drive cattle by nipping their heels.

clue.text: County not in favour of barrier to contain river

indicators.note: the word for opposing holds the letter for river inside it

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: A county opposes building a flood wall to hold back the river.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside CON, then WALL follows. Cornwall is the county at England's far south-west tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornwall is a county in south-west England.

clue.text: Who might be jumping ship, having lost heart?

definitions.text: Who might be jumping ship, having lost heart?

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: ratting is deserting, like rats leaving a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Someone asks who might desert, having lost their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost heart' drops the middle T of RATTING. A rating is a sailor below officer rank, the one who might jump ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a non-commissioned sailor, someone who might desert his vessel.

clue.text: One has to provide food about nine: English obsession

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for providing food is read backwards

parts.note: to feed is to provide food
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone fixated on catering serves dinner at nine, English-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns FEED into DEEF. Idée fixe is French for a fixed idea.
explanation.definitionFit: An idée fixe is a fixed idea that dominates the mind, a fixation.
